input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM ROCm functional and performance parity

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: whether vLLM serving on
AMD Instinct accelerators reaches functional and performance parity with the
productized CUDA builds for the platform's supported model set. It runs a
validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware using upstream ROCm
builds of vLLM and produces the go/no-go scope that determines which models
the productized ROCm serving runtime must support. The deliverable is a
validated campaign report with per-model functional results, performance
parity data against the CUDA baseline, and an explicit cleared/failed model
list.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or partner-lab
  access — see Risks; the access itself is an externally-controlled
  precondition, while standing up the validation environment on secured
  hardware is in scope here).
- Stand up the validation environment on the secured hardware: AMD GPU
  driver stack, ROCm runtime, and upstream vLLM ROCm serving images.
- Define the campaign protocol for the supported model set: per-model
  functional pass/fail criteria and performance parity measurements against
  the CUDA serving baseline.
- Execute the campaign: serve each supported model via vLLM on ROCm under
  the KServe deployment surfaces used by the platform, collecting functional
  and performance data.
- Produce the campaign report: per-model functional results, performance
  parity data, and the go/no-go cleared model list that scopes productization
  of a supported ROCm serving runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The campaign report exists and covers every model in the supported model
  set, with a recorded functional pass/fail result per model.
- The campaign report records performance parity measurements for each
  functionally passing model against the CUDA serving baseline, using a
  documented, reproducible measurement method.
- The campaign report states an explicit go/no-go list of cleared models
  that can be used to scope the productized ROCm serving runtime.
- Each served model in the campaign was exercised through the same KServe
  deployment surface (InferenceService/ServingRuntime) the platform uses in
  production, and the deployment configuration used is captured in the
  report.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of
  the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware access is unresolved and externally controlled: no AMD Instinct
  nodes exist in the CI fleet, and procurement or partner-lab access timing
  cannot be compressed by engineering work. This is an availability
  precondition, not an acceptance criterion; the campaign starts once access
  is secured.
- Upstream ROCm runtime image releases are controlled by AMD and the
  upstream communities; the campaign should pin and record the exact image
  versions used so results are reproducible.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic delivers a supported, productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime for
the models cleared by the AMD Instinct validation campaign. Today only CUDA
(NVIDIA) runtime builds are productized; ROCm builds exist upstream but are
neither shipped nor supported. The epic turns the campaign's go/no-go scope
into a shippable runtime: midstream builds of the vLLM ROCm runtime,
packaging as a ServingRuntime for the platform, and validation that the
runtime serves the cleared models under KServe on AMD Instinct nodes.

## Scope

- Add ROCm build variants of the vLLM serving runtime to the existing
  midstream productization flow (the same flow that ships the CUDA builds).
- Pin the upstream ROCm runtime image/base versions the builds are cut from,
  recording the exact validated digests.
- Define and ship the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime packaging that
  deploys the ROCm vLLM runtime on AMD GPU nodes for the cleared model set.
- Validate serving of each cleared model through the packaged runtime under
  KServe InferenceServices on AMD Instinct hardware (both the functional
  result and the deployment surface used in the campaign).
- Ensure the new runtime image builds and passes the existing build pipeline
  used for serving runtime releases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm serving runtime image is built in the midstream productization
  flow and passes the existing build pipeline (pipeline green on the ROCm
  variant).
- The shipped runtime pins a recorded, validated ROCm image/base version,
  and the pinning is documented in the release metadata.
- A ServingRuntime packaging exists that deploys the ROCm vLLM runtime, and
  each model on the campaign's cleared list serves successfully through a
  KServe InferenceService using that runtime on AMD GPU nodes.
- The runtime is declared supported for exactly the cleared model list, and
  models that failed the campaign are explicitly excluded from the supported
  set.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks / Notes

- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities and may not align with platform release trains; the pinned,
  validated-image approach above is the mitigation. If cadence misalignment
  blocks consuming an upstream image for a target release, the build
  approach is reworked against the nearest available validated upstream
  build.
- The go/no-go scope of this epic (which models are supported) is set by the
  validation campaign's report; if no models clear, this epic's
  productization scope is empty and the epic is removed.
- KServe itself requires no code change for this capability: the runtime is
  deployed through the existing ServingRuntime/InferenceService surfaces.

# PyTorch ROCm training support through the Training Operator

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on ROCm for single- and multi-GPU jobs
executed as PyTorchJobs through the Training Operator. It covers
ROCm-capable training images and the job-level support needed for
multi-GPU (ROCm collective communication) execution, so that distributed
training workloads run on AMD GPU nodes the same way CUDA-based PyTorchJobs
run today.

## Scope

- Provide ROCm-capable PyTorch training images for job execution through
  the Training Operator, including multi-GPU collective communication
  support appropriate to ROCm.
- Validate single-GPU PyTorchJob execution on AMD GPU nodes with ROCm
  images.
- Validate multi-GPU (and, where job topologies require, multi-node)
  PyTorchJob execution on AMD GPU nodes, including gang-scheduled
  admission through Kueue when workload queueing is enabled.
- Fix any Training Operator changes needed for job pods requesting AMD GPU
  resources on ROCm nodes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm training image completes successfully
  on AMD GPU nodes.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm training image completes successfully
  on AMD GPU nodes with multi-GPU collectives functioning (verified by a
  distributed training run).
- PyTorchJobs requesting AMD GPU resources are admitted and run when Kueue
  workload queueing is enabled. This epic's validation responsibility for
  that admission surface is job runnability under queueing (the job, once
  admitted, actually runs on AMD GPU nodes); `amd.com/gpu` quota accounting
  and enforcement are validated by the Kueue quota-handling work, not here.
- The ROCm training images are built and released through the existing
  Training Operator image release flow.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, shared with the Kueue quota-handling work): PyTorch training
  on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through
  Kueue — this epic covers the Training Operator / PyTorchJob execution
  side, with validation responsibility for job runnability under queueing;
  quota accounting and enforcement for `amd.com/gpu` belong to the Kueue
  quota-handling work.

## Risks / Notes

- Validation requires physical AMD GPU nodes with a working ROCm driver
  stack; node availability is an environment precondition shared with the
  serving validation campaign.
- PyTorch ROCm image releases are controlled upstream; image versions
  should be pinned to validated builds.

# Kueue quota handling for AMD GPUs (amd.com/gpu)

## Description

This epic makes AMD GPUs a quota-managed resource in the platform's
queueing layer, so that training jobs requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources
are admitted through Kueue with proper quota accounting — mirroring how
NVIDIA GPU quota is handled today. It covers the Kueue configuration
surfaces (quota flavors and queues) and their validation for ROCm training
workloads.

## Scope

- Define Kueue quota configuration for `amd.com/gpu` resources
  (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota flavors covering AMD GPU nodes).
- Validate that PyTorchJobs and other queueable workloads requesting
  `amd.com/gpu` are admitted, queued, and quota-accounted correctly,
  including all-or-nothing (gang) admission semantics for multi-GPU jobs.
- Fix any Distributed Workloads stack changes needed for correct
  `amd.com/gpu` resource handling in admission and quota accounting.
- Expose queue-level visibility for AMD GPU workloads consistent with
  existing queueing metrics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A ClusterQueue/LocalQueue configuration exists that grants and accounts
  `amd.com/gpu` quota, and a job requesting `amd.com/gpu` within quota is
  admitted.
- A job requesting `amd.com/gpu` beyond its queue's quota is held pending
  (not partially admitted), demonstrating correct quota enforcement.
- A multi-GPU training job is admitted with all-or-nothing semantics —
  either all requested AMD GPUs are granted or the job waits.
- Admission and quota behavior for AMD GPU workloads is validated with
  queueing enabled on a cluster with AMD GPU nodes. This epic's validation
  responsibility for that admission surface is `amd.com/gpu` quota
  accounting and enforcement; whether the admitted jobs themselves run
  correctly is validated by the PyTorch ROCm training-support work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, shared with the PyTorch ROCm training-support work): PyTorch
  training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted
  through Kueue, with `amd.com/gpu` quota handling — this epic covers the
  Kueue quota/admission side, with validation responsibility for
  `amd.com/gpu` quota accounting and enforcement; job runnability under
  queueing belongs to the PyTorch ROCm training-support work.

## Risks / Notes

- Validation requires a cluster with AMD GPU nodes exposing the
  `amd.com/gpu` resource (device plugin and node provisioning are cluster
  infrastructure outside this strategy's components).
- Configuration-level validation can largely proceed against the existing
  quota model; only final admission validation needs live AMD GPU nodes.

# Document AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement: hardware, drivers, validated models

## Description

This epic authors the customer-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm)
enablement: which AMD hardware is supported, the driver prerequisites for
serving and training on ROCm, the validated model list, and how to configure
quota for AMD GPU workloads. The content reflects what was actually built
and validated — the productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime, the PyTorch
training support, and the campaign's validated model list.

## Scope

- New documentation topics covering:
  - Supported AMD hardware (Instinct accelerators) for serving and training.
  - Driver and ROCm runtime prerequisites for AMD GPU nodes.
  - The validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, including
    explicitly unsupported (failed-parity) models where relevant.
  - Configuring Kueue quota for `amd.com/gpu` training workloads.
  - Installing and using the ROCm serving runtime through the platform's
    serving stack.
- Content is authored through the Red Hat docs content process and
  technically reviewed against the implemented and validated behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the supported AMD hardware and the driver
  prerequisites for both serving and training on ROCm.
- Published documentation states the validated model list, matching the
  go/no-go scope established by the validation campaign and the supported
  set of the productized runtime.
- Published documentation covers quota configuration for AMD GPU training
  workloads admitted through Kueue.
- All new content is technically reviewed against the implemented
  behavior by engineers from the implementing teams, with review sign-off
  recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list.

## Risks / Notes

- Content depends on the outcomes of the validation campaign and the
  implementation work; authoring cannot complete before those deliverables
  exist.
- This epic is gated on the validation campaign: if no models clear the
  parity bar (and the serving-runtime productization work is removed
  accordingly), the productized-runtime usage topic is replaced by
  documentation of the failed-parity outcome and an explicitly unsupported
  model list; the hardware, driver, and quota topics stand as written.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9020

## Strategy Overview

AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training. Two strategic customers
standardize on AMD Instinct accelerators; the platform ships only CUDA runtime
builds and has no first-hand ROCm parity data. The strategy mandates a
hardware validation campaign (HLR-1) whose go/no-go output scopes productizing
a vLLM ROCm serving runtime (HLR-2), PyTorch training support on ROCm through
Kueue (HLR-3), and customer-facing documentation (HLR-4).

## Triage

Not below threshold: the strategy spans four components, two teams, and three
work-product types (validation campaign, code productization, documentation),
with HLRs at three priority levels. Not documentation-only: HLR-1..3 require
code and validation work. Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E001 | AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM ROCm functional and performance parity | Investigation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E002 | Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E003 | PyTorch ROCm training support through the Training Operator | Implementation | Distributed Workloads | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E004 | Kueue quota handling for AMD GPUs (amd.com/gpu) | Implementation | Distributed Workloads | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9020-E005 | Document AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement: hardware, drivers, validated models | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P1 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9020-E001 Validation campaign] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9020-E002 vLLM ROCm runtime productization]
    E001 --> E005[RHAISTRAT-9020-E005 Documentation]
```
